title: Checkout Barrier Index

headlines.label: Median axe-core violations per product page (distinct WCAG A/AA rules failed)
headlines.note: axe-core 4.14.0, tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa, wcag22aa, one product page per store. Median failing elements per product page: 13. Home page median: 3 rules.

headlines.label: Stores where keyboard-only traversal could not reach add to cart within 150 Tabs
headlines.note: Tab only from the top of the page, no Enter, Space or clicks; Escape pressed once if focus was trapped. Counted over product pages with an enabled add-to-cart control named "add to cart/bag/basket" or "buy now". Focus traps among the failures: 1. Not in the denominator: 12 pages where a cookie or sign-up dialog held focus and Escape did not close it, 7 whose add-to-cart button is disabled or hidden until a size is chosen, 8 with no control using that wording, 0 traversal errors.

headlines.label: Stores where Tab alone could not reach add to cart, counting a dialog that held focus as blocked
headlines.note: The same traversal as the row above, but the 12 pages where a cookie or sign-up dialog held focus and Escape did not close it count as blocked instead of being left out: a keyboard or screen-reader user meets that dialog first. Added on 9 November 2026 after the first analysis, from the same crawl; no store was crawled again.

headlines.label: Stores with at least one button that has no accessible name (home or product page)
headlines.note: axe-core rules button-name, input-button-name and aria-command-name. A screen reader announces these as "button" with nothing else.

headlines.label: Most common failing rule: color-contrast
headlines.note: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds. Counted once per store if it fails on the home, product or cart page; 697 failing elements in total. Tied on store count with target-size (480 elements); ranked first by failing elements.

headlines.label: Sampled stores that refused or timed out for an honest, rate-limited, read-only crawler
headlines.note: Blocked at the home page: 21; at the product page: 3. Also excluded: 0 disallowed by robots.txt, 16 with no product page found from the home page, 0 crawler errors. Blocked stores are left out of every other number.

headlines.label: Sightline path: product facts, readback and payment reachable by voice and keyboard on all 60 items; no store UI needed
headlines.note: A design property, not a measurement on these stores: Sightline reads product facts from catalog data, speaks the readback and pays through PayPal, so none of the store pages audited here sit on its path. 60 is the number of stores whose product page was crawled.

limitations: Convenience sample: 100 well-known stores selling everyday goods, picked from public knowledge and platform showcase pages, then grouped by the platform their pages actually showed. Not a random sample of all online stores, and platform groups are small, so per-platform numbers are indicative only.

Crawled between 2026-11-08 20:14 and 2026-11-08 22:07 UTC from a single location in India with headless Chromium at 1280×900. Stores change their pages often, and geo redirects, currency conversion and consent banners differ by country: several large US retailers answered with a country selector or a global corporate page, which shows up here as no product page found.

Stores that timed out or gave no product page on the first pass were crawled once more after product-link discovery was widened (a second category page and flat product URLs). Stores already measured were not crawled again, so a fresh run of the current code can pick different product pages.
24 stores refused or timed out and are excluded, so the measured set leans toward stores without aggressive bot defences.
Automated rules catch only part of WCAG. Zero axe violations would not mean a page is accessible; these counts are a floor, not a full audit. No screen reader was run.
One product page per store, found from links on the home page (or up to two category pages). It may not represent the rest of the catalogue.

Keyboard traversal presses Tab only (plus Escape once when trapped). It never presses Enter, Space or arrow keys, so it does not open menus, choose a size or dismiss dialogs that need a button press. Pages where a consent or sign-up dialog held focus, and pages whose add-to-cart button is disabled or hidden until a size is chosen, are left out of the reachability rate rather than counted as failures.
Add to cart is matched by its accessible name in English ("add to cart/bag/basket", "buy now"). Stores that use other wording are counted as having no matching control, not as failures.

Visible focus is a heuristic: computed styles of the focused element, its label, parent, next sibling, first child and pseudo-elements are compared focused versus blurred. It misses indicators drawn elsewhere and can count unrelated style changes.
Product images, the price region and size or colour selectors are found by heuristics on class names, the main heading and structured data, and can miss or misclassify elements.

Cart pages are opened by direct URL only where robots.txt allows: 32 stores had an (empty) cart page audited and 29 were skipped because robots.txt disallows it, so cart numbers are partial. Checkout pages are never opened.
The Sightline path line is a design property of the product, not a measurement on these stores.

Stores appear only as unsalted 12-character sha256 prefixes of their domain. That keeps names out of the published data but does not stop someone who guesses a domain from confirming it; the per-store rows exist for reproducibility, not for naming stores.

topRules.help: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
All touch targets must be 24px large, or leave sufficient space
Interactive controls must not be nested
<li> elements must be contained in a <ul> or <ol>
<ul> and <ol> must only directly contain <li>, <script> or <template> elements
Zooming and scaling must not be disabled
Certain ARIA roles must contain particular children
